title: AI could 'change the stakes' on bioweapons: UK spy chief
key_facts: Ken McCallum, director general of MI5, Britain's domestic security service, gave the agency's annual threat briefing on Tuesday 13 Oct at its London headquarters.
He said 'Today AI is already supercharging the cybersecurity contest between attackers and defenders'.
He said AI has the 'potential to change the stakes on existing or even new bioweapons'.
MI5 launched a new AI Threat Assessment Centre this year, housed at its headquarters, drawing on expertise from other bodies for assessments that 'separate the bluster from the realities'.
MI5 has uncovered suspects using AI to improve reconnaissance and attacks, including with AI-enabled drones.
He said 'human history has given us no experience of facing an actor which is smarter than we are'.
He also said MI5's state-threats caseload has quadrupled over a decade, that Russia remains 'aggressor number one', and that more than 50 arrests were made in Iran-linked operations over 12 months.
quote_evidence: 'Today AI is already supercharging the cybersecurity contest between attackers and defenders,' Ken McCallum, MI5 director general, said in his annual threat briefing.
Artificial intelligence technology had the 'potential to change the stakes on existing or even new bioweapons', he warned.
'Put at its simplest, human history has given us no experience of facing an actor which is smarter than we are.'
why_it_matters_hint: The head of Britain's domestic security service names AI as a growing security risk and says it has set up a unit to assess it.
